fields.mechanism: Self‑expanding metal lattice (as used in aerospace deployable structures) exerts a constant outward radial force that preserves conduit diameter under external pressure or internal blockage.
fields.intervention: Embed a shape‑memory alloy lattice within the wall of each catheter lumen that self‑expands to a preset diameter after insertion, creating an internal scaffold that resists lumen narrowing while keeping the catheter’s external profile unchanged.
fields.expected_effect: The internal lattice continuously props the lumen open, mitigating fibrin or debris buildup and maintaining target flow rates without enlarging the catheter size.
fields.falsification_test: Perform a simulated occlusion test where catheters with the lattice and control catheters are exposed to increasing concentrations of proteinaceous slurry; record the flow rate decline over time to verify superior patency of the lattice‑enhanced design.

fields.mechanism: Mechanical support of a drainage lumen by a self‑expanding metal stent mesh that maintains lumen patency while the catheter passes through a mesh aperture.
fields.intervention: Incorporate a thin, flared self‑expanding metal mesh sleeve (≤4 mm pore size) around each lumen of the multi‑lumen drainage catheter, allowing the catheter to sit within the mesh so the mesh sustains the lumen diameter without increasing the overall catheter outer diameter.
fields.expected_effect: The mesh scaffold prevents collapse and tissue/fibrin ingress, thereby reducing lumen occlusion and preserving the required flow rate while keeping the catheter’s external size unchanged.
fields.falsification_test: In a benchtop model with simulated fibrin and blood debris, compare flow decay over 72 h between a standard multi‑lumen catheter and the mesh‑reinforced catheter; a statistically significant slower flow loss in the mesh version falsifies the null hypothesis that the mesh provides no occlusion resistance.

fields.mechanism: Self‑expanding metal stent provides a rigid scaffold that restores and maintains lumen patency, allowing a drainage catheter to pass through its mesh without collapse.
fields.intervention: Embed the multi‑lumen drainage catheter within a flared self‑expanding metal stent (or line each lumen with a thin self‑expanding metal mesh) so the stent holds the lumen open while the catheter remains the same outer diameter.
fields.expected_effect: The catheter lumen remains open under physiological conditions, reducing occlusion risk while preserving the required flow rate without increasing overall catheter size.
fields.falsification_test: In a simulated drainage model, compare flow decline and occlusion time of catheters with an internal self‑expanding metal scaffold versus standard catheters when exposed to fibrin/debris under identical pressure conditions.

fields.mechanism: A self‑expanding metal stent provides a rigid scaffold that maintains lumen patency while a catheter is threaded through a mesh pore, creating a protected fluidic channel.
fields.intervention: Integrate a thin self‑expanding metal mesh sleeve around each lumen of the multi‑lumen drainage catheter, with ≥4 mm mesh pores that allow a narrow internal drainage tube to be inserted through the mesh, forming a “catheter‑mesh complex” that resists collapse and occlusion without increasing the overall outer diameter.
fields.expected_effect: The mesh scaffold mechanically supports the lumen, preventing external compression and reducing fibrin or debris buildup on the lumen wall, thereby maintaining the required flow rate while keeping the catheter’s external size unchanged.
fields.falsification_test: Conduct an in‑vitro fouling study where standard catheters and mesh‑reinforced catheters are exposed to protein‑rich, particulate‑laden fluid; measure flow rate over 7 days and compare the time to 50 % flow reduction—significant improvement in the mesh‑reinforced group would support the mechanism.

fields.mechanism: Embedding the drainage catheter within a self‑expanding metal stent mesh pore provides external structural support that maintains lumen patency and resists occlusion.
fields.intervention: Integrate a flared self‑expanding metal stent around the multi‑lumen catheter, routing each lumen through ≥4 mm stent mesh pores so the catheter is anchored within the stent without increasing its external diameter.
fields.expected_effect: The stent‑supported catheter maintains the required flow rate over time, markedly reduces lumen occlusion, and does so without enlarging the overall catheter size.
fields.falsification_test: In a controlled bench test, circulate a fibrin‑rich fluid through two identical multi‑lumen catheters—one standard and one with the stent‑mesh support—and measure flow rate decay and occlusion incidence over 72 hours; a statistically significant slower flow decay in the stented catheter would confirm the mechanism.
